headings.title: Statute of jeofails curing formal omissions and non-prejudicial defects
headings.reviewNote: Lists eighteen formal omissions, misstatements, surplusages, and non-prejudicial defects that do not invalidate an indictment or information or stay/arrest proceedings.

headings.title: Requirement of sufficient notice of offense charged
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section shall render valid any indictment that does not fully inform the defendant of the offense charged.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and 13 case annotations; eighteen non-invalidating indictment/information defects under statute of jeofails and subsection 2 sufficient-notice proviso verified.

headings.title: Joinder of multiple defendants participating in same transaction
headings.reviewNote: Permits charging two or more defendants in the same indictment or information notwithstanding Rule 24.06 when alleged to have participated in the same act, transaction, or series of acts/transactions.

headings.title: Joinder of multiple offenses of same character or common scheme
headings.reviewNote: Permits charging two or more offenses in separate counts notwithstanding Rule 24.07 when of same/similar character, based on same act/transaction, or parts of a common scheme or plan.

headings.title: Prohibition on joint charging upon showing of substantial prejudice
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits charging two or more defendants together if substantial prejudice would result, defining substantial prejudice as real, existing bias or discrimination.

headings.title: Presumption of no substantial prejudice in conspiracy prosecutions
headings.reviewNote: Presumes no substantial prejudice from joint charging or joint trial of defendants charged as joint participants in a section 562.014 conspiracy.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and statutory history; permissive joinder of defendants and offenses notwithstanding Supreme Court Rules 24.06 and 24.07, substantial-prejudice bar and definition, and section 562.014 conspiracy presumption verified.

headings.title: Venue change procedures in counties with large correctional populations
headings.reviewNote: Requires defendants in counties with DOC centers averaging over 2,000 yearly offenders to follow subsections 2 to* 5 (original-rolls footnote: 'through') for misdemeanor or felony venue changes notwithstanding Rule 32.03.

headings.title: Grounds for change of venue for inhabitant prejudice or state influence
headings.reviewNote: Permits ordering a change of venue upon defendant's written application based on inhabitant prejudice or undue state influence.

headings.title: Filing deadlines for change of venue in felony and misdemeanor cases
headings.reviewNote: Sets application filing deadlines at thirty days after arraignment for felonies and ten days before trial date for misdemeanors.

headings.title: Service of application and hearing notice on all parties
headings.reviewNote: Requires service of a copy of the venue application and notice of presentation time on all parties.

headings.title: Form and signature requirements of venue application
headings.reviewNote: Requires application to state reasons and be signed by defendant or attorney, without requiring verification.

headings.title: State denial, evidentiary hearing, and transfer to convenient county
headings.reviewNote: Permits unverified state denial within five days, directs evidentiary hearing if denied, and requires venue transfer to a convenient county if grounds are established, known to court, or uncontested.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 6 subsections, statutory history, and original-rolls footnote ('through'); note catchline names Cole County while subsection 1 uses a >2,000 DOC offender population criterion overriding Rule 32.03.

headings.title: Removal order commanding sheriff to deliver prisoner upon venue change
headings.reviewNote: Requires court or officer granting venue removal for a confined defendant to order the sheriff to deliver defendant and warrant/process to the receiving county jail, subject to subsection 2.

headings.title: Sheriff agreement on jail confinement and transportation responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Permits transferring and receiving sheriffs to agree on which county jail houses defendant (defaulting to receiving county), making the transferring sheriff responsible for timely court transport if retaining custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; prisoner removal order upon change of venue and permissive inter-county sheriff housing agreement with transport allocation verified.

headings.title: Setting case for trial as soon as reasonably possible upon speedy trial request
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to set criminal case for trial as soon as reasonably possible after defendant announces ready and files a speedy trial request.

headings.title: Mandamus enforcement and limitation on dismissal absent constitutional violation
headings.reviewNote: Makes section enforceable by mandamus and bars dismissal for noncompliance or failure to prosecute unless the court also finds denial of constitutional speedy trial right.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and section 217.460 cross-reference; prompt trial setting upon readiness and speedy-trial request, mandamus enforcement, and constitutional-violation requirement for dismissal verified.

headings.title: Mandatory joint trials for jointly charged defendants and consolidation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates joint trials for jointly charged defendants notwithstanding Rule 24.06 and permits consolidation of separate indictments or informations that could have been joined.

headings.title: Mandatory severance upon showing of probability for prejudice
headings.reviewNote: Mandates severance upon defendant's written motion and court finding of probability for prejudice under four enumerated criteria (jury punishment disparity, asymmetric evidence, unlimitable codefendant statement, or fair determination).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and 1954 Castino annotation; mandatory joint trials and permissive consolidation notwithstanding Rule 24.06 and four mandatory probability-of-prejudice severance criteria verified.

headings.title: Mandatory joint trial of jointly charged criminal offenses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates joint trial of two or more offenses jointly charged in an indictment or information notwithstanding Rule 24.07.

headings.title: Severance of offenses upon particularized showing of substantial prejudice
headings.reviewNote: Permits severance of joined offenses or other just relief upon written motion and particularized showing of substantial prejudice (defined as real, existing bias or discrimination).

headings.title: Peremptory challenge entitlements for joint defendants
headings.reviewNote: Entitles each defendant tried jointly under this section to peremptory challenges under section 494.480.

headings.title: Exclusion of character or reputation evidence from definition of evidence
headings.reviewNote: Excludes character or reputation evidence from the meaning of 'evidence' as used in this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, statutory history, and 1966 Lee annotation; note catchline refers to 'persons jointly charged' while subsections 1–2 govern jointly charged offenses notwithstanding Rule 24.07.

headings.title: Court-ordered testing for serious infectious diseases in sex and assault charges
headings.reviewNote: Permits court on prosecutor motion with notice and good cause to order HIV, hepatitis B/C, syphilis, gonorrhea, and chlamydia testing of defendants charged with listed sexual, assault, prostitution, child-endangerment, resisting-arrest, or exposure offenses, sealing records and releasing results to victim and counsel.

headings.title: Definition of HIV
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'HIV' as the human immunodeficiency virus that causes acquired immunodeficiency syndrome.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, transfer/effective-date note (formerly 566.135, eff. 1-01-17), and 3 footnotes noting transferred (565.060/565.070) and repealed (565.075/565.081–565.083) cross-references; permissive testing order and HIV definition verified.

headings.title: Prohibition on copying or distributing recordings of child sexual offense victim
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits defendant, counsel, or defense agents from copying or distributing visual/aural recordings or photographs of alleged minor chapter 566 victims held by assessment centers, providers, or multidisciplinary teams without court order after notice, hearing, and safety/privacy review.

headings.title: Authorized attorney inspection and viewing without furnishing copies
headings.reviewNote: Permits defense counsel or agents to allow defendant, witnesses, or prospective witnesses to view provided materials without allowing them to have copies.

headings.title: Mandatory protective provisions in court orders authorizing copying
headings.reviewNote: Requires any court order authorizing copying or distribution to restrict use to pending proceedings, bar further reproduction/distribution, and mandate return or destruction affidavit upon final disposition.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and statutory history; prohibition on copying/distributing child sexual-offense victim recordings without good-cause court order, defense viewing allowance, and mandatory protective order terms verified.
